title: Considerations-Based Synthetic Respondents and the Bisbee et al. (2024) Baseline: ANES 2024 Feeling Thermometers
summary: Compares two ways of generating synthetic ANES 2024 feeling-thermometer ratings with an LLM persona: direct generation following Bisbee et al. (2024), and a considerations-based pipeline after Zaller (1992) that samples 4 of 8 respondent-specific considerations into each response. Across 100 respondents, 8 targets and 2 draws, the baseline has slightly lower error (RMSE 23.5 vs 24.8; r 0.77 vs 0.74); the considerations pipeline has smaller mean bias (-0.04 vs 2.86) and a smaller average gap in target means (4.3 vs 5.1 points).

methods: Direct persona-conditioned thermometer generation (Bisbee et al. 2024 prompt, updated for 2024)
Zaller 8->4: 8 ranked considerations per respondent and target, 4 sampled into each response draw
design.benchmark: Observed ANES 2024 Time Series pre-election feeling thermometers for the same respondents
metrics: mean and SD gaps by target
total variation and Wasserstein-1 distance between raw draws and observed ratings
design.model: Gemini Flash (generateContent API, alias gemini-flash-latest as of April 14-15, 2026); 2 draws per respondent and target
design.unit: respondent x target x draw (1,600 rows per method; 798 with a valid observed rating)
